_comment: The drafting standards this package knows, as data. A drawing office's own standard is a
project file named in acadmcp.json's `standards` list; its rows merge over these ones, so
it restates only what it disagrees with.
Two rules govern every row here, and they are the point of the file:
* a transcribed number carries `source` — the standard and the table it was read from;
* a table nobody has transcribed ships EMPTY, and a lookup in it refuses by name
('not transcribed') instead of interpolating a neighbouring value. Nothing in this
file was recalled from memory, and no value here is guessable from the others.
Tables: layers, text_heights, line_width_groups (the 0.7 group transcribed; the 0.5b row
and every other b value are still pending), scales (a pointer at sheet.SCALES, never a
second copy), title_block, and gbt50103's own dimensioning (the metres rule alone).
A standard may also set `extends` to name ONE parent standard: the parent's resolved tables
merge under the child's own rows, so a specialised standard restates only its deltas.

standards.name: gbt50001
standards.label: GB/T 50001 房屋建筑制图统一标准

layers._source: layers.LAYERS — the colour and linetype every layer is drawn with, read off the reference drawing's scheme and mirrored here so a project file can restate one row instead of all of them.
layers._note: The lineweight column is pending transcription. No line width in this repository has been read off GB/T 50001, so every row states `null` — a layer with no width set draws ByLayer, which is what this package drew before the standard became data. A drawing office transcribes its own b-series into its project standards file; a lookup in a table nobody has transcribed refuses by name rather than being interpolated.

text_heights._source: GB/T 50001 图纸字高名义系列 — heights on the sheet, in millimetres, not heights in the model.
text_heights._note: A model height is a paper height times the plot scale's denominator: 3.5 mm on a 1:100 sheet is 350 mm in the model. That conversion is the checker's and is deliberately not written here, because a table of model heights per scale would be a second place for one fact to live.

line_width_groups._source: GB/T 50001 线宽组 — b, 0.7b, 0.5b, 0.35b — and the b series. The b series is read from secondary sources (题库 pages quoting the standard) and is stated the same way everywhere; the 0.7 group's widths are 用户提供设计院规范文档 图面基本规范 (依 GB/T 18229)'s 粗 0.7 / 中粗 0.5 / 细 0.25.
line_width_groups._note: Two readings of the group rows are in circulation and this file does not choose between them: sources give an A0 sheet's group as 1.4:1.0:0.7:0.35, which reads as rows b/0.7b/0.5b/0.25b, while the standard's own row names are b/0.7b/0.5b/0.35b (0.35b of 1.4 is 0.5, not 0.35). Resolve against the standard's own table before relying on a row above b=0.7. A lookup in a row nobody transcribed refuses by name rather than being interpolated.

0.7.source: 用户提供设计院规范文档 图面基本规范 (依 GB/T 18229)

scales._note: A pointer, not a copy. sheet.SCALES is the one list of ratios this package plots from, and a second copy here would be a second thing to keep in step — so Standard.scales returns that list rather than this table.

title_block._source: GB/T 10609.1 标题栏. These are this package's defaults for a Chinese architectural sheet; a drawing office has its own, the same way it has its own layers.

symbols._source: GB/T 50001 常用符号 — the conventional sizes, read from secondary sources (题库/百科 pages quoting the standard) rather than from the standard's own text. Recorded here so a project can restate a row and so a divergence from what this package actually draws is visible instead of assumed.
symbols._note: No tool draws from this table. It is the sourced record kept beside the ops' own constants (ops.LEVEL_TRIANGLE_MM, NORTH_ARROW_DIAMETER_MM, NORTH_ARROW_TAIL_MM, SECTION_TICK_MM) so the two can be compared. Where a source is self-contradictory it is recorded as such, not resolved by picking one.

level_mark.source: 题库 (引 GB/T 50001): '标高符号应以等腰直角三角形表示,用细实线绘制,高约3mm'

north_arrow.source: 题库 (引 GB/T 50001), stated identically by several: '指北针外圆用细实线绘制,圆的直径为24mm,指针尾部宽度为3mm' — one source says 圆用粗实线 instead; unresolved.

section_mark.source: 题库 (引 GB/T 50001), several agreeing: '剖切位置符号长度为6-10mm,剖切投射向符号长度为4-6mm'

index_mark.source: 360百科 剖面详图索引符号: '索引符号由直径为10mm的圆和其水平直径组成,圆及其水平直径均应以细实线绘制'

grid_bubble.source: 题库 (引 GB/T 50001): '定位轴线应用细单点长划线绘制,轴线编号应注写在轴线端部圆圈内,圆圈应用细实线绘制,直径为8-10mm'

fonts._source: GB/T 14691-1993 技术制图 字体 — read from secondary sources (题库) quoting the standard.
fonts._note: The ratio is what makes 长仿宋体 long: 字宽 = 字高 / √2. No backend sets a width factor today (every text style is drawn at XScale 1.0), so text drawn by this package is wider than the standard's face. The table records the rule; giving the backends a width factor is separate work.

long_fangsong.source: 题库 (引 GB/T 14691-1993): '长仿宋体的字高与字宽比例为√2:1(约1.414:1)'

dimensioning._source: 用户提供设计院规范文档 总平面布置图节 (依 GB/T 50103-2010)
dimensioning._note: Only the metres rule is transcribed. The decimals figure and the site-plan layer names are still pending transcription from the standard text itself, so no site-plan layer row is added here — the names would have to be invented, and a standard's layer names are the drawing office's to state (this standard inherits gbt50001's layer rows and nothing else). Nothing formats a dimension from this table yet: today it is data a lookup may refuse on, not behaviour.

layers._source: lineweights: 用户提供设计院规范文档 图面基本规范 (依 GB/T 18229) 的线宽组 (the 0.7 group of gbt50001/line_width_groups); colour and linetype: gbt50001/layers, restated row by row because a child row replaces its parent's whole row, not just the fields it states.
layers._note: The mapping onto the layers is this package's, not the document's: 0.7 (b) for A-WALL and for the sheet's frame — 图框为粗实线, the document's 图幅与图框节依 GB/T 14689 — 0.5 (0.7b) for the openings, the structure and the cores, and 0.25 (0.35b) for the pattern, the annotation and the sheet's own text. The widths are the document's; a drawing office restates the rows it draws differently in its project standards file. text_heights is deliberately not restated: the document's 2.5–10 series is a subset of the one inherited from gbt50001.
